distinguishing_features: Uses a high-gradient magnetic field to physically capture paramagnetic/ferromagnetic iron and thorium-bearing particles rather than altering operating setpoints or dosing chemistry
Introduces no reagent dose and no filter media; separation is by magnetic force on the particle
Targets capture of sub-50 µm fines that gravity/bag filtration misses, exploiting F=(χV/2μ₀)∇(B²) exceeding drag
Applied to rare-earth leachate impurity separation, a different stream and failure mode than brine/digester scaling or bed agglomeration
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Remove fine iron-bearing and thorium-bearing particulates/colloids from a rare-earth leachate stream without adding reagents or consumable filter media, and without the clogging and poor sub-50 µm capture of gravity or bag filtration.
parsed.viable_reason: WHIMS/high-gradient magnetic separation is an established, physically sound industrial process whose force-balance (magnetic vs drag) supports capturing fine magnetic particles, and it is implementable at the stated scale.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: None of the prior art (brine scaling-control dosing, digester antiscalant setpoint, fumed-silica bed agglomeration) employs magnetic-gradient capture, so applying HGMS to this leachate impurity problem is not a routine extension of the closest art.
